result.output:
1	# Build, release, and the docs site
2	
3	## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly
4	
5	- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
6	[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
7	- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
8	  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
9	  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
10	  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
11	- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
12	  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.
13	
14	## The gate
15	
16	- `pnpm run ready` — build `-r`, `vp check`, test `-r`, markdown lint. Must pass before you're done.
17	- `pnpm run check:publish` — `publint`.
18	- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
19	  `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
20	- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
21	  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
22	  creating package tags.
23	- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
24	  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
25	  `ready` runs `vp run -r build` before `vp check`, so generated files exist in order.
26	
27	See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
28	organization governance model.
29	
30	## Linting CSS
31	
32	Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
33	`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
34	`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
35	`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.
36	
37	## The docs site
38	
39	`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
40	(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
41	set a custom `i18nRouting`).
42	
43	- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
44	  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
45	  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
46	  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
47	- **Block-level API translation.** `build-api-locales.ts` doesn't translate whole `.md` files — it
48	  runs `segment-markdown.ts` to split each generated page into blocks: `prose` (descriptions,
49	  remarks, `@example` captions, cssdoc table Description cells), `glossary` (section headings,
50	  stability-badge pills, table column labels), and `preserve` (code fences, signatures, breadcrumbs,
51	  token tables). Only prose carries a content key, so a page's prose survives the scaffolding churn
52	  (badge flips, token-value changes, signature edits) that used to bust a whole-file key. `glossary`
53	  blocks always go through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (keyless, never cached);
54	  `preserve` blocks are emitted verbatim.
55	- **The committed cache carries the prose; CI serves it.** The translation memory
56	  (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and adapter-agnostic, so a claude-authored
57	  prose entry is served to a `glossary` build as a plain cache hit. The workflow: run
58	  `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` **locally** to author prose (a cold run is bounded to ~30–40
59	  batched `claude -p` calls, resumable via the memory's autosave), then commit `hu.api.json`. CI's
60	  `docs:build` runs the `glossary` adapter, which serves that prose from cache and only ever fills
61	  structural headings/labels. Brand-new prose that isn't cached yet passes through as English — the
62	  glossary **never** caches its own prose passthrough (that would permanently mask the block from a
63	  later claude run), so it stays a miss until claude authors it. Never wire `:claude` into CI.
64	- **Running the cold pass.** Each `claude -p` call cold-starts a full agent, and the dominant cost is
65	  the per-call bootstrap — loading MCP servers, plugins, and project settings — not the translation
66	  itself (it dwarfs even a small model's inference). So the `:claude` tasks pass
67	  `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user`: a fast model, **no
68	  MCP**, and user settings only (keeps auth, drops project/local hooks). That cuts each call from
69	  minutes to a few seconds. Override by editing the task or exporting your own
70	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` before a direct `node scripts/…` run (`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`
71	  overrides the `claude` binary itself). Either task logs progress (`… N/M labels + prose blocks
72	translated`) and saves the memory after **each** chunk, so it's resumable — a kill or crash keeps
73	  completed chunks and a re-run serves them from cache.
74	- **The cold pass is generation-bound, so it runs chunks concurrently.** Once MCP is stripped, the
75	  wall-clock cost is the model streaming translations, not startup — so `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter`
76	  runs up to `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 5) `claude -p` calls at once. Prose is batched at
77	  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_BATCH_BUDGET` chars/request (default 4k) — small enough that each JSON response
78	  stays reliable and progress is fine-grained, with the pool hiding the per-call startup. A chunk that
79	  errors is logged and skipped (its blocks stay uncached and retry next run), never sinking the whole
80	  run. Raise concurrency for more speed if you're not rate-limited; lower the budget if a run trips the
81	  per-item fallback (the model dropping a key from a large response).
82	
83	## The cssdoc integration
84	
85	pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
86	workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
87	(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
88	and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
89	`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
90	`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.
91	
92	**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
93	catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.
94	
95	## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation
96	
97	Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
98	that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
99	direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:
100	
101	- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
102	  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
103	- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
104	- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
105	  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
106	  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.
107	
108	A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
109	script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.
110

# Optimize commit / publish / release / docs / CI

## Context

The commit→release→publish→docs toolchain has one glaring gap and several redundancies:

- **No PR CI.** The only `pull_request` workflow (`changeset-check.yml`) just checks that a
  changeset exists. Build / typecheck / test / lint / gates run **only** at release-tag time
  (`release.yml`) — so broken code can merge to `main` and first fail during a docs deploy or a
  release. This is the biggest risk.
- **commitlint is dead config.** `commitlint.config.ts` + two `@commitlint/*` devDeps exist, but the
  `commit-msg` git stage is a no-op (no `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` file) and nothing in CI checks
  messages. Conventional commits are unenforced.
- **`release.yml` double-works.** `cut-release.ts` already runs build/check/test + publint + attw
  **scoped to the release set** before tagging; the pushed tag then re-runs the **full-workspace**
  `ready` + `gate:publint` + `gate:attw`, sequentially, regardless of release size.
- **`docs.yml` over-builds and over-deploys.** It runs on every push to `main` with no path filter
  and rebuilds the whole workspace (`vp run -r build`), even for pushes that don't touch the site.
- **`ready` is a fully sequential 7-step `&&` chain**; independent lint/validate steps never overlap.

Goal: add the missing PR gate, enforce conventional commits, and cut the redundant/sequential work —
without breaking the `vp`-only CI constraint (no pnpm on PATH) or publish provenance.

### Verified mechanics (load-bearing)

- vp's task cache is `node_modules/.vite/task-cache/` and stores task **outputs** as `.tar.zst`
  tarballs — so a cache **hit re-materializes the gitignored generated files** (`platforms/**/generated/`,
  `formats/components/generated/`, web-components `src/generated/`, etc.). This is why downstream jobs
  can replay `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a full rebuild.
- `vp run -F "<pkg>..." <task>` selects the package **and its dependencies** (pnpm-style closure;
  confirmed in `vp run --help`: `<pattern>...` = deps, `...<pattern>` = dependents, `<pattern>^...` =
  deps only). So the docs build can be scoped to `@pantoken/docs`'s subgraph.
- Git hooks: `core.hooksPath=.vite-hooks/_` (vp-managed, gitignored dispatcher). Human hook bodies live
  at `.vite-hooks/<name>`. The `_/commit-msg` dispatcher already exists and forwards `$1`, and `_/h`
  prepends `node_modules/.bin` to PATH — so dropping in `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` is auto-wired, no
  installer step.

---

## 1. New PR CI gate — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Trigger: `pull_request` + `push` to `main`. Concurrency cancels superseded PR runs:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

**Job graph** — one `build` job warms the cache, everything else fans out `needs: build` so no cold
stampede. The union of jobs equals `ready` + publint + attw, parallelized; `ready` itself is never
called in CI.

- `build` (no `needs`): checkout → setup-vp → **cache save** → `vp run -r build`.
- `typecheck` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` (cache-extract) → `vp check`.
- `test` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run -r test`.
- `lint` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `lint:css`, `lint:js`,
  `validate:generated:only`, `lint:markdown` (sequential within the job; all cheap).
- `publint` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run gate:publint`.
- `attw` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run gate:attw` (slowest; isolated so it
  doesn't gate the others).
- `commitlint` (independent, PRs only): `fetch-depth: 0` → setup-vp →
  `vp exec commitlint --from ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} --to ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} --verbose`.

Every job: `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1` with `cache: true, run-install: true` (the only install step;
provides `vp`, no pnpm needed).

**vp task-cache persistence** — path is the single subtree, restored **after** setup-vp so install
can't clobber it. The cache is content-addressed internally, so a stale restore only yields misses,
never wrong output.

- `build` job: `actions/cache@v4`, path `node_modules/.vite/task-cache`,
  key `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml','vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}`,
  restore-keys `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml','vite.config.ts') }}-`
  then `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-`.

- **New `.vite-hooks/commit-msg`** (committed, executable, no shebang — runner invokes `/bin/sh -e`,

exactly the release set. Reorder so the release-plan step runs **first** (it already emits
`.release-packages.txt` and `.release-plan.json`), then drive scoped gates from it:

- `vp run -F <release-set> build && vp run -F <release-set> check && vp run -F <release-set> test`
- `vp exec -F <publishable-set> publint` and the existing scoped `attw` invocation.

Build the `-F` list from the release plan (the full release set for build/check/test so packs are
complete; the publishable subset for publint/attw). Add the task-cache **restore** so the scoped build
hits `main`'s warmed cache. **Leave every publish/provenance step unchanged**: `setup-node` registry,
corepack pnpm, `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, `id-token: write`, the publish loop, the GitHub release.

Safety tradeoff (accepted): release.yml stops re-verifying packages outside the release set — that
coverage now comes from `ci.yml` on the merge-to-main that produced the tag, plus `cut-release.ts`
locally. What actually ships to npm is still gate-verified against the exact publish set immediately
before publish.

## 4. Optimize `docs.yml`

- **Path filter** so a deploy only runs when the site can actually change. Add `on.push.paths`
  (broad-but-correct, since the site is themed by generated token output from many packages):
  `docs/**`, `packages/**`, `formats/**`, `platforms/**`, `renderers/web-components/**`, `plugins/**`,
  `design/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; keep `workflow_dispatch`.
- **Scope the build** from `vp run -r build` → `vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build` (docs + its
  dependency closure), skipping native/platform packages docs doesn't consume. Then the existing
  `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build`.
- **Add the task-cache restore** (same config as ci.yml) so unchanged deps are cache hits.
- Keep `concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }` (don't cancel a live publish).

## 5. Parallelize `ready` + cleanups

- **Make `ready` a vp task DAG** so `vp run ready` parallelizes locally too. In `vite.config.ts`
  `run.tasks`, define leaf tasks and a `ready` that `dependsOn` them, with the independent gates all
  depending on the recursive build:
  - `check:all` → `vp check`, `test:all` → `vp run -r test`, reuse existing `lint:css`/`lint:js`/
    `validate:generated:only`/`lint:markdown`.
  - `ready` → `command: "true"`, `dependsOn: ["check:all","test:all","lint:css","lint:js","validate:generated:only","lint:markdown"]`;
    each leaf `dependsOn: ["<recursive build>"]`.
  - Update root `package.json` `"ready"` to `vp run ready`. vp then runs the independent leaves
    concurrently after build.
- **`check:publish` should include the types gate.** Add `gate:publish` = publint + attw (or make
  `check:publish` run both), and update `AGENTS.md` / `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` which cite
  `check:publish` as "the gate" but omit attw.
- **`cut-release.ts` micro-cleanup**: `packageHasScript` shells out to `spawnSync("cat", …)` per
  package × 3 tasks — replace with `fs.readFileSync` (or reuse the manifests already loaded by
  `loadWorkspacePackages()`), at `scripts/release/cut-release.ts:385`.

### Deferred (noted, not doing now)
- Centralizing the duplicated 9-root workspace-glob list (`vite.config.ts` gate tasks ×2,
  `changeset-check.yml` paths ×1, `PACKAGE_ROOTS` in `workspace-packages.ts`) — cross-tool (YAML↔TS)
  sharing is awkward; low value.
- Parallelizing the sequential `pnpm publish` loop in `release.yml` — low value, sequential is safer
  for provenance/ordering.

---

## Critical files

- **New**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.vite-hooks/commit-msg`
- **Edit**: `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, `vite.config.ts`

  (`release.yml`) — so broken code can merge to `main` and first fail during a docs deploy or a
  release. This is the biggest risk.
- **commitlint is dead config.** `commitlint.config.ts` + two `@commitlint/*` devDeps exist, but the
  `commit-msg` git stage is a no-op (no `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` file) and nothing in CI checks
  messages. Conventional commits are unenforced.
- **`release.yml` double-works.** `cut-release.ts` already runs build/check/test + publint + attw
  **scoped to the release set** before tagging; the pushed tag then re-runs the **full-workspace**
  `ready` + `gate:publint` + `gate:attw`, sequentially, regardless of release size.
- **`docs.yml` over-builds and over-deploys.** It runs on every push to `main` with no path filter
  and rebuilds the whole workspace (`vp run -r build`), even for pushes that don't touch the site.
- **`ready` is a fully sequential 7-step `&&` chain**; independent lint/validate steps never overlap.
- **`gate:repository` only runs at release time.** It landed on `main` after npm OIDC/trusted-publishing
  provenance broke — publishable `package.json`s lacked `repository.url`, which provenance requires.
  `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts` now asserts every publishable manifest has
  `repository.url === "git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git"`, wired into `release.yml`
  (`vp run ready && gate:repository && gate:publint && gate:attw`, sequential). But it's the *last*
  place to catch the exact failure that broke production, and it's a pure manifest read (no build) — so
  it belongs at PR time too.

and cut the redundant/sequential work — without breaking the `vp`-only CI constraint (no pnpm on PATH)
or publish provenance.

- vp's task cache is `node_modules/.vite/task-cache/` and stores task **outputs** as `.tar.zst`
  tarballs — so a cache **hit re-materializes the gitignored generated files** (`platforms/**/generated/`,
  `formats/components/generated/`, web-components `src/generated/`, etc.). This is why downstream jobs
  can replay `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a full rebuild.
- `vp run -F "<pkg>..." <task>` selects the package **and its dependencies** (pnpm-style closure;
  confirmed in `vp run --help`: `<pattern>...` = deps, `...<pattern>` = dependents, `<pattern>^...` =
  deps only). So the docs build can be scoped to `@pantoken/docs`'s subgraph.

name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay
  # `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a cold rebuild.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:

      - name: Set up Vite+

        with:

          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache

    steps:

        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:

      - name: Set up Vite+

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

input.new_string:
# Plan first: this emits release_packages / publish_packages / publish_count to GITHUB_OUTPUT,
      # which the scoped gate and publish steps read. cut-release.ts already ran the full scoped gates
      # locally before tagging, and ci.yml ran the whole `ready` on the merge-to-main this tag points
      # at — so here we verify a clean build + types + tests, then scope the pack-heavy publish gates to
      # exactly what ships. (Non-publish lint/validate/markdown are covered by ci.yml, not repeated.)
      - name: Build package release plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          node scripts/release/plan-package-release.ts \
            --tag "${RELEASE_TAG}" \
            --json .release-plan.json \
            --publish-list .release-packages.txt \
            --markdown .release-plan.md

      - name: Verify release gates
        shell: bash
        run: |
          vp run -r build
          vp check
          vp run -r test
          vp run gate:repository

          # publint/attw pack each package and are the dominant gate cost — scope them to the publish
          # set. `vp exec -F` runs the bin per matched package (no "task not found" like `vp run -F`).
          filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra publish_pkgs <<< "${{ steps.plan.outputs.publish_packages }}"
          for pkg in "${publish_pkgs[@]}"; do

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
  `lint:js`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
  race). Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
  ran on the merge-to-main the tag points at).
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.

| Csomag                                                                                  | Mihez csatlakozik                                                                             |

Több pantoken csomag generál fájlokat a build során — egy stíluslapot, egy `theme.json`-t, egy beágyazott token
modult. A repó tisztán tartása és a kimenetek megbízhatósága érdekében minden csomag ugyanazt a konvenciót követi, és
egy workspace feladat validálja az egészet.

## A `generated/` konvenció

Minden csomag, amely build műterméket állít elő, egy csomagonkénti `generated/` könyvtárba írja azt, és
semmi más nem él ott. Egyetlen szabály a `.gitignore` fájlban mindet lefedi:

```txt
**/generated/
```

Így nincs commitolt generált fájl — a build újra előállítja. Kétféle kimenet kerül oda:

- **Szállítható statikus fájlok** — olyan fájlok, amelyeket a felhasználó importál, például `@pantoken/css` `style.css` fájlja vagy
  `@pantoken/scss` `tokens.scss` fájlja. A csomag `exports` leképezése megtartja a nyilvános kulcsot
  (`"./style.css"`), de a `generated/` helyre mutat, így a fogyasztói API sosem változik.
- **Build köztes fájlok** — olyan fájlok, amelyeket a csomag saját forrása importál és bundlingol a `dist` mappába, például
  `@pantoken/tokens` beágyazott JSON-ja. Ezeket önmagukban nem publikálják; be vannak fordítva.

## A kimenet validálása

A `@pantoken/validate-generated` (egy privát eszköz) fut a build után, és három dolgot ellenőriz:

1. minden generátor csomag ténylegesen írt egy nem üres `generated/` könyvtárat,
2. a `pantoken` CLI legalább egy fájlt generál minden támogatott célra, és
3. egyetlen generált stíluslap sem tér el a token IR-től — `danglingReferences` az önálló
   lapokhoz, és `unknownReferences` a hidakhoz, amelyek csak máshol definiált tokenekre hivatkoznak.

## Parancsok

```sh
# Rebuild every package, regenerating all generated/ output.
pnpm run generate

# Rebuild, then run the validator.
pnpm run validate:generated
```

## What I did

Everything's on branch `optimize-ci-release-hooks` (I branched off `main`, no commits yet).

**1. New PR CI gate — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (was missing entirely)
Parallel jobs — `build` → `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus independent `repository` and `commitlint` jobs. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`); `build` warms it, downstream jobs restore and re-materialize generated dirs from the tarball cache. PR runs cancel superseded runs.

**2. Conventional-commit enforcement**
New `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` → `vp exec commitlint --edit "$1"` (auto-wired via the existing dispatcher), plus the `commitlint` CI job over the PR commit range. The commitlint config was dead before.

**3. Faster `release.yml`**
Plan runs first (emits the publish set), then a clean build/typecheck/test + unscoped `gate:repository`, with the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` scoped to just the packages being published. Dropped the redundant full `ready`. All publish/provenance steps untouched.

**4. Leaner `docs.yml`**
Path filter (no deploy on unrelated pushes), scoped build `vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build` (docs subgraph, not the whole workspace), and the persisted cache.

**5. `ready` parallelized + cleanups**
`ready` is now a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`): `build:all` runs once, then six gates fan out concurrently. I funneled all generation through `build:all` to avoid a real cold-cache codegen race. Folded `gate:repository` + `publint` + `attw` into `check:publish`. Replaced a `cat` subprocess in `cut-release.ts` with `readFileSync`. Updated `AGENTS.md`, `build-and-docs.md`, `architecture/overview.md`.

Let me answer the release-tag question first, since it affects your plan — then dig into the three docs changes.

## Will a tag cut on the PR branch trigger the release workflow?

**Yes, it triggers it — but the tag won't be "on main," and that's the problem.** Git tags are refs to a commit, independent of branches. `release.yml` fires on `push: tags: "@pantoken/*@v*"` regardless of which branch the commit lives on, and it checks out the tagged commit (not main). So:

- A tag pushed from `optimize-ci-release-hooks` **will** run `release.yml`, building/publishing from the **PR-branch commit**, not main.
- If the PR is later **squash-merged**, main gets a *different* SHA. The tag stays pointing at the orphaned PR-branch commit — so the published version's commit isn't in main's history, and the root `CHANGELOG.md`/tag chronology won't line up with main.

Two other things worth flagging before you cut:

- **`@pantoken/docs` is `private: true`** — not publishable. Cutting it produces an empty publish set, so `release.yml` would run the gates, then **skip publish and skip the GitHub release** (`publish_count == 0`). It wouldn't actually exercise the npm publish path. If you want to test publishing, pick a publishable package; if you want to test the docs *site*, that's `docs.yml` (push to main), not `release.yml`.
- **Cleanest test paths:** either merge this PR to main and cut from main, or cut a **prerelease** (`--beta`/`next` dist-tag) to exercise the pipeline without touching `latest` — accepting the tag won't be on main until merged.

My recommendation: merge to main first, then cut a real (or `beta`) release from main. Want me to hold the release until merge?

## Root cause

The Hungarian API sidebar links are **not** locale-prefixed. The labels get translated to Magyar, but every `link` still points at the English `/api/...` tree instead of `/hu/api/...`.

I confirmed this empirically: `docs/hu/api/typedoc-sidebar.json` has **592 links starting with `/api/`** and **0 starting with `/hu/`** (e.g. line 16: `"link": "/api/tools/aggregate/src/interfaces/Target.md"` under the translated `"text": "Cél"`).

## 1. Where sidebar `link` values are set, and whether they're locale-prefixed

There are two distinct sidebar sources per locale, built in `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`:

**Guide + nav sidebar — correctly prefixed.** Built inline (lines 128–167) using `locale.guidePrefix` / `locale.apiPrefix`. For `hu` these are `/hu/guide/` and `/hu/api/` (from `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts` lines 132–133), so guide/nav links are correct. Example (config.ts:140–142):
```ts
{
  text: locale.sidebar.gettingStarted,
  link: `${locale.guidePrefix}getting-started`,
},
```

**API (TypeDoc) sidebar — NOT prefixed (the bug).** Loaded from a pre-generated JSON file, not built from prefixes (config.ts:67–76):
```ts
const loadSidebar = (relativePath: string): DefaultTheme.SidebarItem[] => {
  const sidebarPath = fileURLToPath(new URL(relativePath, import.meta.url));
  return existsSync(sidebarPath)
    ? (JSON.parse(readFileSync(sidebarPath, "utf8")) as DefaultTheme.SidebarItem[])
    : [];
};

const typedocSidebarByLocale = Object.fromEntries(
  localeEntries.map(([localeKey, locale]) => [localeKey, loadSidebar(locale.typedocSidebarPath)]),
) ...
```
For `hu`, `typedocSidebarPath` is `../hu/api/typedoc-sidebar.json` (i18n.ts:150). That JSON's `link` values are all `/api/...`, so they leak the English locale even though the section is registered under `[locale.apiPrefix]` = `/hu/api/` (config.ts:172).

## 2. Shared once vs. generated per-locale

Mixed. The TypeDoc sidebar JSON *is* generated per-locale by `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`: it clones `docs/api` → `docs/hu/api` (lines 120–122) and translates the sidebars. But the per-locale pass only translates the `text` labels — it never touches `link`. See `translateSidebar` (build-api-locales.ts:67–79), which recurses on `text` and `items` only:
```ts
const translateSidebar = (item: SidebarItem, translate: (text: string) => string): SidebarItem => {
  const translated: SidebarItem = { ...item };
  if (translated.text) {
    translated.text = translate(translated.text);
  }
  if (translated.items) {
    translated.items = translated.items.map((child) => translateSidebar(child, translate));
  }
  return translated;
};
```
And the rebuild loop (lines 180–183) writes back only the label-translated tree. So the HU sidebar is per-locale for labels but effectively shares English links.

## 3. Exact file + line where the fix goes

Best fix — in `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`, in the sidebar rebuild loop at **lines 180–183**:

Confirmed, with the exact mechanism. The CI run is fully green now, and here's the `pack` diagnosis:

## Why `pack` misses in CI but not locally

Every miss says the same thing:

```
vp pack ○ cache miss: 'node_modules/.modules.yaml' modified, executing
```

- vp caches each package's `build` script (the repo uses `cache: true`, which enables script caching). The **compile** steps hit (`node scripts/generate.ts ◉ cache hit`), because they track *source* files.
- But `vp pack` auto-tracks the files it reads, which includes pnpm's **`node_modules/.modules.yaml`** (the installed-module manifest — pack resolves workspace deps through it).
- Every CI job runs `setup-vp` with `run-install: true`, and that reinstall **rewrites `.modules.yaml`**. So the pack fingerprint changes in every job → guaranteed miss. Locally there's no reinstall between runs, so pack replays from cache (we saw `vp pack ◉ cache hit` twice).

So: **build's compile is cached; `pack` is invalidated by the per-job reinstall, not by anything in your code.**

## What I found for fixing it — and my recommendation

I checked vp's config surface. There's **no global input-exclude knob** — `run.cache` only has `scripts`/`tasks` booleans. You *can* exclude `!node_modules/**` from a task's `input`, but only on `run.tasks` entries, and these are 70 per-package `build` *scripts*, not tasks. Converting all of them isn't worth it.

The two "real" fixes both lose:
- **Cache `node_modules` across jobs** (so `.modules.yaml` is stable): node_modules here is 1,129 packages — tarring/uploading/restoring it per job almost certainly costs *more* than the ~30–50s of repacking it saves. Net-negative.
- **Pass built `dist` as an artifact** instead of rebuilding downstream: eliminates the repack, but it's the brittle "enumerate every gitignored `generated/`/`dist` across 9 roots" approach the cache was chosen to avoid.

My recommendation: **accept it.** The repack is ~0.3–0.7s/package and the jobs run in parallel, so it's ~30–50s on the critical path of the full-build jobs. And the scoped-build change I just added means on a *typical* (non-global) PR, `attw`/`publint` only build the changed closure — so they barely repack at all. This PR looks expensive only because it changes root `package.json` (`scope: all`).

Want me to leave it, or pursue the `dist`-artifact approach for the always-full jobs (`typecheck`/`test`/`lint`)?

CI is running on the final push. I've verified everything locally end-to-end, so let me summarize where things stand.

## PR [#5](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/5) — complete, 10 commits

**The original scope (all landed and locally verified):**
1. **PR CI gate** (`ci.yml`) — parallel jobs (build → typecheck/test/lint/publint/attw + repository + commitlint), persisted vp task cache.
2. **Conventional commits** — `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook + CI `commitlint` job.
3. **Scoped `release.yml`** — plan-first, publint/attw scoped to the publish set, provenance untouched.
4. **Leaner `docs.yml`** — path filter, `-F "@pantoken/docs..."` build, cache.
5. **`ready` → parallel task DAG** (`ready:all`).

**Added along the way, from your prompts:**
6. **Scoped `publint`/`attw` to what a PR changes** (`changed-packages.ts` + tests), and scoped their build to that closure.
7. **Pack-cache fix** — the real win from your `pack` catch: every CI reinstall rewrote `node_modules/.modules.yaml`, busting `vp pack` on all ~70 packages every job. Promoted each `build` to a task that excludes that manifest from the fingerprint. Verified: `vp pack ◉ cache hit` survives a `.modules.yaml` touch.
8. **Fixed two pre-existing release-gate bugs** the new CI surfaced — a stale bootstrap changeset naming a non-workspace package, and `changeset-check` unable to diff without the base branch.

**Docs-i18n (this-PR, your three items):**
9. **Sidebar links** → 592 `/hu/api` links, 0 English `/api/` leaks. **Overview** fully Hungarian (`# API referencia`, `## Kezdd itt`, `Terület | Leírás`, translated cells, `/hu/api/…` links). **Drift check** (`check-locale-drift.ts`) — detects untranslated prose/guide blocks, adapter-free, gated in `docs:build`; `docs:locales:translate` fills it locally.

One thing to flag: I ran the local `:claude` pass to author the 13 new overview sentences (that's the `+13` in `hu.api.json`) so the drift gate is green — **you may want to eyeball that Hungarian** since it's machine-authored.

## Your open decision: the release

As covered earlier — a tag cut on this branch *would* trigger `release.yml`, but from the PR-branch commit, not main (and if squash-merged, the tag orphans off main's history). Also `@pantoken/docs` is private, so "releasing" it publishes nothing. My recommendation stands: **merge this PR to main first, then cut a real (or `beta`) release from main.**

content.text: Now rewrite docs.yml — workflow_run trigger + manual dispatch, a path-filter gate, artifact reuse, and the self-building escape hatch:

input.content:
name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed,
# reusing the packages CI already built (downloaded as an artifact) instead of rebuilding the
# workspace. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch — it builds the assets fresh (for a
# `[skip ci]` commit, or to re-run a failed deploy), since the CI artifact won't exist for it.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The site is themed by generated token/CSS output from many packages, so treat those as
          # deploy-worthy too (broad but correct). Compare the pushed commit to its parent.
          if git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -qE '^(docs/|packages/|formats/|platforms/|renderers/web-components/|plugins/|design/|pnpm-lock\.yaml|pnpm-workspace\.yaml)'; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "should_deploy=false" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            echo "No docs-relevant changes in this push; skipping deploy."
          fi

  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.should_deploy == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      # Post-CI: reuse the workspace CI already built. Landing the artifact in place means the site
      # build below has the generated token/CSS output and the docs subgraph's dist without a rebuild.
      - name: Download build output from CI
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # Manual escape hatch: the CI artifact doesn't exist, so build the docs dependency closure fresh.
      - name: Generate token output
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build

      - name: Build docs
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/

      - name: Write custom domain file
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

## Summary

**PR #6 — gate docs behind CI + reuse its build:**
